faqs.question: Can I use AWS Free Tier with Vultr simultaneously?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can use both simultaneously. AWS Free Tier provides 750 hours/month of t2.micro or t3.micro instances for 12 months, plus free storage and data transfer limits. Vultr has no free tier but starts at $2.50/month. Many developers use AWS Free Tier for learning while running production workloads on Vultr’s predictable pricing. faqs.question: Does Vultr offer managed Kubernetes like AWS EKS?
faqs.answer: Yes, Vultr offers Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE) with straightforward pricing starting at $10/month for control plane plus worker node costs. AWS EKS charges $0.10/hour (~$73/month) just for the control plane, plus separate EC2 instance costs. VKE is simpler to configure but lacks EKS’s advanced features like Fargate integration and extensive AWS service integrations. faqs.question: Can I transfer my Reserved Instances from AWS to Vultr?
faqs.answer: No, AWS Reserved Instances are commitment-based pricing contracts specific to AWS and cannot transfer to other providers. If migrating from AWS to Vultr, you’ll need to let your Reserved Instance term expire or sell it on the AWS Reserved Instance Marketplace. Plan migrations carefully to avoid paying for unused AWS commitments while running Vultr infrastructure. faqs.question: Which provider offers better database performance for high-traffic applications?
faqs.answer: AWS RDS generally outperforms Vultr Managed Databases for high-traffic applications due to Multi-AZ deployment with automatic failover, read replicas across regions, and Performance Insights for query optimization. However, AWS RDS costs significantly more. A db.m5.large starts around $175/month versus Vultr’s comparable managed database at $60/month. For applications under 10,000 concurrent connections, Vultr’s performance-to-price ratio is superior.
